mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past three months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past three months (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering a short-term sell-off in equities with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a shift in consumer spending from durable goods to services, which is a positive signal for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST decline and RSAFS rise occurs in more than 50% of cases without positive 20-day returns (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When manufacturing production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (2017=100), it signals a contraction in industrial output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days during a recessionary regime.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) over the past six months signals robust residential construction activity, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST shows sustained upward trend (increase ≥1% over 6 months), 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 3.5%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A deceleration in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a labor market weakening under monetary tightening, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS growth deceleration and FEDFUNDS rise occurs in more than 50% of cases without negative 20-day returns (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly real GDP growth (GDPC1) turns negative, it confirms a recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days during a recessionary regime.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth rate is negative, 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for sign test) or Rank IC over rolling 3-year window < 0.03.
